$comment: CN-016 / D21. The origin-vs-library/ divergence AS MEASURED, so the gate fails when it CHANGES rather than being red on the day it was written. Rule: the measured divergence must EQUAL this file. A new entry is drift nobody chose; a stale entry means the situation improved and the line should be deleted. Both are red, both print the exact edit. 🟢 EMPTY AGAIN FROM 2026-09-11, AND THAT EMPTINESS IS THE POINT. This file had carried a backlog since 2026-08-22 — five rows, then six, every one of them the same fact: an entry authored here and never published, because publishing was a person copying library-dist/ into the docs repo by hand. v0.2.3 shipped six such parts and its release notes carried a caveat admitting nobody could install them. LIB-007 replaced the manual copy with .github/workflows/publish-library.yml, and its first run (NodeGX 52578dd78 → nodegx-content cf873c1e3) published all six. Verified against the SERVED index, not against this repo: prefabs 42→46, modules 30→32, `library:verify-origin --require-published` exit 0. 🔴 AN EMPTY `unpublished` IS NOW THE NORMAL STATE, so a row appearing here again means something was authored and the publish workflow was not run — not a backlog to live with. The reachability question has its own instrument (`--require-published`, which does NOT read this file); this one still answers only "has the divergence changed?". Keeping them separate is LIB-007's finding: a baseline that records "not published yet" cannot also be the thing that tells you to publish. ⚠️ The next growth step this gate owes (per verify-origin.ts §When LBR-001 lands) is a payload-hash check comparing published zips against a fresh build — coverage-by-label is still the only thing checked. Measured on the first CI publish and worth knowing before anyone builds it: `library:build` is NOT byte-reproducible. That publish rewrote 74 already-published zips whose CONTENT was identical — verified by extracting old and new and diffing the trees — because the ZIP last-modified fields carry build time. A naive hash check would call every entry drifted on every run; it has to normalise timestamps, or the build has to stop writing them. Regenerate with `npm run library:verify-origin -- --update-baseline` and say WHY in the commit.
